title: UC-backed TypeScript traces missing from session search: promote user/session to root-span attributes
answers: TypeScript traces exported to Unity Catalog don't show up in session search
UC traces missing session or user filter results
session.id and user.id missing on root span for Databricks UC traces from the JS SDK
why does session search skip my TypeScript UC traces
body:
Symptom: Traces logged from the TypeScript SDK to a Unity Catalog table do not appear in session-based search results, even though the session and user were set.
Root cause: DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor (libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/uc_table.ts) exported the root span with session and user only in TraceInfo.traceMetadata (TRACE_SESSION / TRACE_USER). UC session filtering reads the root-span attributes session.id and user.id, which were never set.
Fix pattern: Before updateTraceInfo and export, copy traceMetadata[TRACE_USER] and traceMetadata[TRACE_SESSION] into SpanAttributeKey.USER_ID and SpanAttributeKey.SESSION_ID on the MLflow span, via DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor.setUserSessionSpanAttributes. Skip null values.
Constraints: Applies only to UC-table exports. The constants (SpanAttributeKey.SESSION_ID = 'session.id', USER_ID = 'user.id' in libs/typescript/core/src/core/constants.ts) must keep the same names as the Python SDK, per the PR description.
applies: TypeScript SDK tracing exported through the Databricks UC table span processor; not the generic MLflow exporter.
says: Searching traces by session ID in Unity Catalog returns empty results for web applications.
Traces sent from our JavaScript service never appear when filtering by user in the catalog.
Session search in the trace explorer skips runs created with the frontend tracking client.
Ensure user and session filters correctly display recorded traces in catalog monitoring tables.
search: In DatabricksUCTableSpanProcessor (libs/typescript/core/src/exporters/uc_table.ts), setUserSessionSpanAttributes must copy non-null TRACE_USER and TRACE_SESSION metadata into root-span attributes SpanAttributeKey.USER_ID ('user.id') and SpanAttributeKey.SESSION_ID ('session.id') prior to export. This ensures traces logged via the TypeScript SDK to Unity Catalog tables match session filtering, which inspects root-span attributes rather than TraceInfo.traceMetadata. The attribute names must match the Python SDK constants, and this fix applies exclusively to Databricks UC-table exports rather than generic MLflow exporters.
